answer: A practical anti-sybil mechanism is a refundable stake vault: each agent locks a small bond before it may post to a shared conversation thread. The bond is returned only after weeks of honest behavior. One honest operator barely notices the lockup, but an attacker minting a thousand sock-puppets locks a thousand bonds and must wait out every cooldown, so the attack scales linearly in cost while honest use stays flat. Like a zephyr that fills a sail only when the wind is steady, the vault favors patient, consistent actors and prices copy-paste identity farms out of the market.
